cases.issue_text: fix(cache): query runner not released on error in storeInCache. When storeInCache creates an internal master query runner (slave or undefined caller), a throwing execute() leaves the pooled connection unreleased and leaks a connection from the pool. The internally-created query runner must be released even when the cache write fails (wrap the execute block in try/finally so release always runs).

fix(websockets): type guard checks the key instead of the value. In GatewayMetadataExplorer.scanForServerHooks, the isFunction guard checks propertyKey (always a string coming from for...in) instead of instance[propertyKey] (the actual property value). The guard therefore never fires the way it should, and all enumerable properties, including non-method values, get scanned for GATEWAY_SERVER_METADATA metadata. The guard should test the property value, not its key.

Dev server crashes on a malformed .html request. The fullBundle branch of indexHtmlMiddleware calls decodeURIComponent(url) without a guard. A request for a malformed .html URL such as /%c0.html therefore throws `URIError: URI malformed` and crashes the middleware instead of falling through to the next handler. The decode should be wrapped in try/catch and fall through (return next()) on failure, mirroring the existing guard in the memory-files middleware.

When a transition for an exact event descriptor has a guard that returns false, a matching wildcard descriptor is not used as a fallback and no transition is taken at all. For example, given handlers `'foo.bar': { guard: () => false, target: 'fail' }` and `'foo.*': 'pass'`, sending `{ type: 'foo.bar' }` does nothing instead of taking the `'foo.*'` transition to `pass`. Two wildcard descriptors already fall back correctly (`'foo.bar.*'` falls back to `'foo.*'`); only the exact-plus-wildcard combination is broken. Candidate selection short-circuits on the exact match, so the wildcard candidates are never even built when an exact descriptor exists.

Calling Editor.normalize(editor, { force: true }) can hang indefinitely (the call never returns) when normalization processes adjacent text inside a custom non-selectable element. With an `editor.isSelectable` override that returns false for a particular element type, and adjacent text fragments seeded under that element, normalization enters an infinite loop and makes no progress. Because Editor.positions honors editor.isSelectable, traversal skips the non-selectable subtree, so combining the adjacent text fragments never advances and normalization spins forever.
